sop-from-memo.output:
# Water Heater Swap

You will need
Main water shutoff valve · Breaker box · Garden hose · Floor drain · New water heater · New flex water lines · Air-bleed faucet (closest to heater) · Camera or phone for photo · Van

Steps

1. Shut off water at the main valve (do not rely on the tank's isolation valve alone).

2. Switch off the breaker serving the water heater.

3. Run the garden hose from the van to the floor drain and drain the tank completely.

4. Disconnect the old water heater from its water lines and electrical connection.

5. Remove the old unit and position the new water heater in place.

6. Install new flex water lines to both inlet and outlet, even if old lines appear intact.

7. Fill the new tank with water.

8. Open the closest faucet to the heater and let air bleed out until water runs steady (no sputtering).

9. Turn the breaker back on.

10. Wait 20 minutes, then inspect all connections and the floor around the unit for leaks.

11. Take a photo of the installed unit and file it with the work record.

Done looks like
Heater is full and holding pressure. All flex connections are hand-tight and dry. Faucet nearest the heater runs clear water with no air. Breaker is on. Photo is filed. Job ticket shows completion time and no callbacks within 48 hours.

Common mistakes
Powering on before the air is bled — water won't flow to upper fixtures and the new heater may cavitate. Check by opening a faucet upstairs before turning the breaker back on.

Ignoring the expansion tank if a check valve is on the main line — pressure will build beyond the tank's capacity and cause leaks or ruptures. Ask owner which main line setup this customer has before starting.

Trusting the tank's isolation valve instead of the main shutoff — water will still drain down into the tank from the supply line and complicate disconnection. Always shut the main first, every time.
